sections.what_happened: Saudi Arabia has postponed its flagship Future Investment Initiative (FII10, 'Davos in the Desert') — scheduled Oct 26-29, 2026, the 10th edition — to 2027; new date 'very soon'; registrations/partnerships stay valid. Cause given publicly is delivering 'full scale, quality and impact'; AFP/WSJ/WSJ-reporter sources tie it directly to Ansar Allah attacks: Riyadh's King Khalid airport (a repeated target) suspended operations after the Oct 10 strike that killed at least 13 (Reuters/WSJ figure; Korean nocutnews citing 'up to 18' — conflict noted) and wounded 300+; >45% of departing Saudi flights canceled since Oct 8 (Cirium); Western travel warnings multiplied; JPMorgan/Citi bankers were canceling, Dimon and Fraser teams debated attending. Expected speakers: BlackRock's Larry Fink, JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon, Goldman Sachs' David Solomon, StanChart's Bill Winters, Citi's Jane Fraser. Al Jazeera reports government staff ordered to work from home. Earlier plan for hybrid/land-route attendance was scrapped.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (announcement + prior exclusive), AFP via CNA/Vanguard, Al Jazeera (cancellation + WFH), The National (postponement, attendees), WSJ via NYPost (Dimon/Fraser teams, airport casualty figures), CNA update 09:15AM Oct 20, Korean Yonhap/nocutnews (Cirium flight data).
sections.what_disputed: Casualty toll on Oct 10 airport strike varies: 13 killed per Reuters/WSJ; 'up to 18' per nocutnews (uncorroborated). Organizers do not explicitly name Ansar Allah attacks as the reason — attribution of motive comes from AFP sources/WSJ reporting, not the official statement. The WFH order for government staff is reported only via Al Jazeera's headline/dek so far.
sections.why_matters: While Washington and Tehran posture, the Ansar Allah just did what sanctions couldn't: they forced Riyadh to cancel 'Davos in the Desert' — the crown jewel of MBS's Vision 2030 pitch to global capital — pushing it to 2027. Riyadh's airport still suspended after the deadliest strike on the kingdom in a decade, Brent back above $110, oil flows through Hormuz cut to ~8.5mbpd: Iran-side framing — the air campaign over Yemen has not stopped Ansar Allah long-range strikes, and the costs are landing in Riyadh's own pocketbook.
sections.context: Background: Saudi Arabia postpones FII 'Davos in the Desert' flagship investment conference to 2027 amid Ansar Allah attacks (Oct 26-29 event scrapped; announcement confirmed Oct 19 by FII Institute)

totw_analysis: Our read: While Washington and Tehran posture, the Ansar Allah just did what sanctions couldn't: they forced Riyadh to cancel 'Davos in the Desert' — the crown jewel of MBS's Vision 2030 pitch to global capital — pushing it to 2027. Riyadh's airport still suspended after the deadliest strike on the kingdom in a decade, Brent back above $110, oil flows through Hormuz cut to ~8.5mbpd: Iran-side framing — the air campaign over Yemen has not stopped Ansar Allah long-range strikes, and the costs are landing in Riyadh's own pocketbook. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the Ansar Allah missile campaign actually breaking Saudi Arabia's economy — or is postponing 'Davos in the Desert' a prudent pause while the kingdom negotiates? Audiences split between 'Vision 2030 is unraveling' and 'the money will still come'; the 13 dead at Riyadh airport and >45% flight cancellations fuel the unraveling side.
